title: Constant-distortion Steiner point removal
formal: Does every weighted graph with designated terminals have a suitably reweighted minor on exactly those terminals whose terminal distances lie between the original distances and a universal constant times those distances?

sentences: Steiner point removal starts with a weighted graph and a designated set of terminals whose mutual distances matter.
The goal is to delete the other vertices through graph-minor operations, leaving a graph on exactly those terminals.
Its edges may be reweighted, but terminal distances should never shrink and should grow by at most a universal factor.
The same guarantee must work regardless of how many terminals the input contains.
This asks whether graph topology and useful terminal geometry can both survive an extreme reduction in representation size.
